question: What does the route of transmission describe in epidemiology?

options.A: The path a pathogen takes from its source to a susceptible host
options.B: The specific time it takes for symptoms to appear in a patient
options.C: The genetic makeup of an infectious agent inside the body
options.D: The method used to destroy microorganisms on medical equipment

explanation: The route of transmission specifically traces the journey of an infectious agent from a reservoir to a new host. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: Why must nurses understand the different pathways of pathogen movement?

options.A: To choose appropriate infection control precautions and prevent outbreaks
options.B: To identify the microscopic structure of various bacterial strains
options.C: To determine the exact financial cost of treating hospital illnesses
options.D: To accurately calculate drug dosages for systemic viral infections

explanation: Knowing how pathogens spread allows nurses to select the correct barrier methods and stop transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: What represents the natural habitat where a pathogen multiplies?
explanation: A reservoir provides the essential environment for an infectious agent to live, grow, and multiply. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: Stopping the spread of disease requires what action regarding the chain of infection?

options.A: Simultaneously eliminating all six links completely
options.B: Focusing solely on destroying the infectious agent
options.C: Targeting only the portal of entry in patients
options.D: Breaking any single link in the chain

explanation: Infection control relies on interrupting the sequence at any point to halt transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: What is an inanimate object that transfers infectious agents called?
explanation: A fomite is any inanimate object capable of carrying and transferring infectious pathogens from one person to another. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: A nurse uses a blood pressure cuff on an infected patient and examines another without wiping it down first. What type of transmission has occurred?
explanation: Using a contaminated device between patients without disinfection represents indirect contact via a fomite. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: Which transmission route requires the use of an N95 respirator mask?
explanation: Airborne pathogens require specialized respiratory protection like N95 masks to filter out tiny suspended particles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between droplet and airborne transmission?

options.A: Whether the source of the infection is an animal or a human
options.B: The presence of fever in the infected person during the exposure period
options.C: Particle size and how long the infectious agent stays suspended in the air
options.D: The specific part of the human respiratory tract invaded by the pathogen

explanation: Droplets are large and fall quickly over short distances, while airborne particles are small and stay suspended longer. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: Which organism typically acts as a vector for transmitting malaria?
explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes serve as the biological vector for transmitting the malaria parasite to humans. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h5)

question: What defines a zoonotic infection in public health?

options.A: An illness caused by inhaling dust particles containing fungal spores
options.B: A disease that spreads naturally from vertebrate animals to humans
options.C: A pathogen passed between humans through contaminated surgical instruments
options.D: An infection acquired exclusively through contaminated drinking water supplies

explanation: Zoonotic diseases originate in animal populations and can cross the species barrier to infect people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h5)

question: What is a common vehicle for transmitting the cholera bacterium in communities?
explanation: Cholera spreads primarily through water and food sources contaminated with infected fecal matter. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: Why is common vehicle transmission capable of causing large outbreaks quickly?

options.A: Infectious agents always travel much faster through liquids than air
options.B: A single contaminated source exposes many people at the same time
options.C: People infected show symptoms within minutes of initial exposure
options.D: The pathogens involved do not require a susceptible host to multiply

explanation: A shared source like a water supply or blood product can infect large populations simultaneously. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure to prevent hospital-acquired infections?
explanation: Regular and proper handwashing or sanitizing removes transient flora and stops cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h7)

question: How do routine immunization programs help control the spread of infectious diseases?

options.A: By destroying pathogens directly on environmental surfaces
options.B: By completely eliminating the natural animal reservoirs of viruses
options.C: By building community herd immunity to block pathogen circulation
options.D: By curing patients of chronic bacterial infections rapidly

explanation: Vaccines protect individuals and reduce the pool of susceptible hosts, stopping transmission chains in populations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h7)
